title: Today's rundown
note: What's going on right now, in one place. Want the full story on one of these? Say so in the comments below — enough interest turns an item into its own entry.

items.text: President Trump addresses the UN General Assembly on September 22 — his first appearance since the US entered its war with Iran seven months ago — as the second speaker after Brazil's Lula da Silva, three days after announcing a new US-Greenland-Denmark security agreement.

The Palestinian Health Ministry says Israeli strikes and gunfire have killed 1,394 Palestinians and injured 4,839 in Gaza since the ceasefire began in October 2025, with 834 of the dead still under rubble.

The Federal Reserve raises its benchmark rate a quarter point to 3.75%-4% on September 16, its first hike since 2023, citing persistently elevated inflation; the FOMC votes 12-0 and its projections leave room for another increase this year.

Brent crude falls to about $100 a barrel on September 21, a fourth straight session of declines, as traders bet on diplomatic de-escalation between the US and Iran ahead of this week's UN General Assembly.
Bitcoin opens at $86,597.82 on September 22, up 6.7% from Monday's open, before slipping as much as 2.2% to $85,092 following Monday's eight-month high of $87,381.
Russia's central bank proposes capping banks' crypto-asset exposure at 1% of capital, the same week South Korea's Hana Bank issues a $100 million digital bond through Euroclear's blockchain platform.

AMD's stock hits an all-time high of $613.92 on September 21, pushing its market cap past $1 trillion for the first time and making it the fourth US chip company — after Nvidia, Broadcom and Micron — to cross that threshold; the stock is up more than 180% this year.

Security researchers disclose "Plugin4Shell" on September 18, a zero-click remote-code-execution flaw letting attackers swap malicious plugin code past SHA-pinning checks in Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot and Gemini CLI; Anthropic patches it in Claude Code 2.1.179, OpenAI in Codex 0.146.0.

Healthcare distributor McKesson discloses a cybersecurity breach detected August 25 involving unauthorized access to third-party applications, with the ShinyHunters extortion group claiming to have exfiltrated 284 million rows of patient data from its Oncology & Multispecialty and Medical-Surgical units.

Astronomers confirm Elias 2-24 b, a Jupiter-mass planet less than a million years old orbiting a star 450 light-years away, as the youngest planet ever found — the previous record-holders were all at least 5 million years old — in work led by Andrea Bernardi, a doctoral candidate at Universidad Diego Portales in Chile.
Indonesia's Anak Krakatau erupts for more than 24 hours starting September 4, sending ash as high as 50,000 feet, shutting down eight airports and disrupting nearly 3,000 flights.

SpaceX's Super Heavy booster arrives at the pad on September 21 ahead of Starship Flight Test 14, targeting September 28 for the vehicle's first orbital launch attempt, carrying 26 V3 Starlink satellites.

A UK Biobank study of 11,071 adults finds nighttime light exposure above 3 lux is linked to thickening of the heart's left ventricle wall and early signs of reduced cardiac function three years later, in research led by Tulane University's Lu Qi and published September 9 in the European Heart Journal.

A Washington University School of Medicine study of more than 333,000 veterans with type 2 diabetes finds cardiovascular risk climbs the longer patients stay off GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy after stopping — 4% higher at six months, 14% at one year, 22% at two years — with the lost benefit not fully restored even after resuming treatment.
